ledger.note: 1274: the Duchy of Jawor is formed out of Legnica. 'established in 1274 as a subdivision of the Duchy of Legnica'; Henry V is its first duke (granted by his father in 1273 per the Henry V page) and gives it to his younger brothers Bolko I and Bernard when he succeeds in Legnica in 1278.
1281: Bernard becomes Duke of Lwówek. 'In 1281 Bernard was made a Duke of Lwówek.'
1286: Bolko I inherits Lwówek from Bernard and reunites the lands.

region.text: the 12 cells Cliopatria's Jawor shape adds in 1305: Świdnica, Strzegom, Strzelin, Ziębice and Ząbkowice Śląskie

ledger.note: 1291: Bolko I receives Świdnica and its towns. 'Bolko I received Świdnica, Strzegom, Strzelin, and Ziębice from Henry V, by receiving the Duchy of Świdnica'; those lands had been part of the Duchy of Wrocław, which Henry V gained after Henry IV Probus died in 1290. Cliopatria draws the growth only from 1305.

region.text: Bolesławiec and Chojnów, the districts Bolko I of Jawor took while Henry III was at Krzywin and Henry III renounced in March 1297

ledger.note: March 1297: Bolko I keeps Bolesławiec and Chojnów. 'When Henry III stayed in Krzywin, Bolko I took Chojnów and Boleslawiec'; after the settlement at Zwanowice of March 1297 the Duke of Głogów 'managed to make a truce with the Duke of Jawor, but was forced to renounce the above-mentioned districts' (Henry III page). The Jawor page says only that Bolko I 'acquired Chojnów from Duke Henry III of Głogów', undated. Cliopatria's Jawor shape of 1305 holds 1 cell at Bolesławiec and 2 at Chojnów; the 1279 shape holds 1 cell at Chojnów and the Legnica shapes also draw both towns, so the keyframes are left as they are. Mirror of the Głogów dossier's loss.

region.text: the 12 cells Cliopatria's Jawor shape adds in 1305: Świdnica, Strzegom, Strzelin, Ziębice and Ząbkowice Śląskie

ledger.counterpart: Duchies of Świdnica and Ziębice (Bolko I's sons)
ledger.note: 1312: Bolko I's sons divide the lands. 'Jawor went to Henry I, and Świdnica and Ziębice became separate duchies again.' Cliopatria keeps the Świdnica cells in the Jawor shape to 1313.

region.text: Jawor of Henry I, the duchy's last drawn shape after the Świdnica and Ziębice cells left in 1312

ledger.note: 1313: the last Cliopatria shape of the Duchy of Jawor. The duchy itself lasted: Henry I expanded west in 1319 (Zgorzelec, Lubań, Żary), Bolko II reunited Jawor with Świdnica in 1346 and 'was the last Piast duke to retain his independence' from Bohemia (d. 1368); it was 'finally annexed by the Bohemian Crown' in 1392. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bohemia covers the land from 1314; the year is the map's, the page is silent.

wars.name: Support of Bolko I of Jawor for Henry V the Fat against Henry III of Głogów
wars.outcome: Henry V gave Bolko the Świdnica lands in 1291 'in return for his support against Henry III'; no land is recorded as fought over in Jawor itself.
wars.note: The Jawor page does not mention the war; the Henry V page is the source.

certainty.note: The duchy's frontiers are lists of towns and castellanies; the page gives no treaty boundary (its infobox gives the western limit as Zły Komorów for 1319, outside the map).

notes: Cliopatria's Jawor row begins in 1279 although the duchy began in 1274; keyframes _1274 and _1291 are added. Cliopatria's shape of 1279-1304 is 4 cells (1,099 km2) and stays so until 1305 although Bolko I received Świdnica in 1291; the growth is dated 1291 from the page. The Jawor page does not date the vassalage to Bohemia (1292, 1329, 1337 not mentioned) and says only that Wenceslaus II backed Henry V in the Wrocław dispute; the duchy outlived the map (annexed to Bohemia 1392) and the additions batch eu-15-x is to cover the Polish duchies after 1304. The Silesia dossier carries a matching loss to duchy-of-jawor in 1290-1291. The wars list cites a quotation from the Henry V page, a page opened for the Legnica dossier. Gazetteer lacks Jawor and Lwówek Śląski (circle by coordinates, from the town, not from the page). Counterparts without a dossier: Duchy of Lwówek (Bernard), Duchies of Świdnica and Ziębice (small, inside this duchy's story). Repair pass of 2026-10-31 (reviewer findings): the 1305 shape is cut to 1305-1311 and the Cliopatria 1279 shape (Henry I's Jawor) is drawn for 1312-1313 after Bolko I's sons divide the land in 1312; Bolko I's keeping of Bolesławiec and Chojnów in March 1297 is a gain from duchy-of-g-ogow (the Głogów dossier has the matching loss).
